/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 40-year-old woman presents with difficulty falling asleep, diminished appetite, and tiredness for the past 6 weeks. She says that, despite going to bed early at night, she is unable to fall asleep. She denies feeling anxious or having disturbing thoughts while in bed. Even when she manages to fall asleep, she wakes up early in the morning and is unable to fall back asleep. She says she has grown increasingly irritable and feels increasingly hopeless, and her concentration and interest at work have diminished. The patient denies thoughts of suicide or death. Because of her diminished appetite, she has lost 4 kg (8.8 lb) in the last few weeks and has started drinking a glass of wine every night instead of eating dinner. She has no significant past medical history and is not on any medications. Which of the following is the best course of treatment in this patient?

Options:
A. Diazepam
B. St. John’s Wort
C. Paroxetine
D. Zolpidem
E. Trazodone

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question concerns diagnosis and treatment of a depressive disorder with insomnia, which falls within psychiatry and mental health."}
